title: Error Budget Flighting & Forecast Tracker for Reliability Initiatives
creator: Maya Rivera
description: Build an initiative-level tracker that forecasts error budget burn for active rollouts and flighted experiments, surfaces at-risk initiatives to PMs/Eng leads, and proposes mitigation steps. This feature ties SLI ingestion, burn-rate forecasting, and the roadmap/OKR tracker together so product teams can: 1) see time-to-exhaustion forecasts for each initiative, 2) flag initiatives with >50% chance of exhausting error budget within next 7 days, 3) run automated or suggested mitigations (traffic rollback, reduced concurrency, fallback routes) and 4) capture a decision trail for postmortems and OKR reviews. Scope: console UI components + backend forecasting service + normalized SLI pipeline and per-initiative metadata. Key constraints: maintain low alert noise, preserve SLO signal integrity across services, and avoid adding heavy query load to production services.
acceptance_criteria:
1) Console: new Initiative Forecast tab shows time-to-exhaustion, projected burn rate, and recommended next actions for each active initiative.
2) Backend: forecasting job runs hourly with max 6-hour data lag and stores 90-day history.
3) Alerts: automated at-risk alerts created when forecasted exhaustion < 7 days or probability > 50%.
4) Mitigations: UI exposes safe rollback/scale-down links and records actions in the initiative timeline.
5) Cross-team: at least two teams onboarded to pilot (Runtime and Console) and feedback captured in a retrospective doc.
success_metrics:
- Forecast accuracy (MAE) <= 7 days over 30-day horizon for pilot initiatives.
- Reduction in emergent rollback incidents by 30% for flighted rollouts.
- Time-to-detect SLI degradation reduced from median 2h to 45min.
- 75% of at-risk alerts have an acknowledged action within 1 hour during pilot.
decision_log: 2026-02-22: Chose hourly forecasting job (compromise between freshness and compute cost).
2026-02-25: Forecast model approach: EWMA + trend-dampening heuristic selected over full ARIMA for simplicity and explainability. Will revisit if pilot error is high.
2026-03-02: Aggregation window standardized to 5m for ingestion, 1h for forecasting input. Trade-off: higher noise vs load; will add smoothing if noisy metrics observed.
2026-03-08: Auto-mitigation threshold set to 30% of remaining error budget; below that, UI prompts for manual rollback and suggestions only (no automatic traffic changes in pilot).
rollout_plan: Phase 1 (pilot): enable for Runtime and Console teams, backfill 90 days of SLI history, run forecasts in dry-run mode and surface predictions in a read-only console (2 weeks). Phase 2 (controlled actions): enable action links + ack flow for engineers (4 weeks). Phase 3 (wider rollout): add more teams, tune thresholds, and enable optional automation if pilot shows low false positives (Q2 rollout).
notes: Stakeholders: Maya Rivera (PM lead), Ethan Chen (Eng lead), Priya Nair (SRE advisor), Jonah Park (Console designer).
Blocker: ENG-2123 (SLI normalization library) must land before accurate cross-service forecasts—securing priority on their sprint.
Risk: Forecasting can produce false positives during noisy deployments; mitigation is to add ensemble smoothing and human-in-the-loop ack.
Next steps: finalize ingestion schema, schedule kickoff with Runtime/SRE on 2026-03-12, spin up a demo dashboard for pilot data by 2026-03-20.
